mentl/d90598e:
Per CLAUDE.md anchor 8 (cascade discipline), walkthrough first.
Resolves design questions before any cache/driver code lands.

Key decisions captured:

  KaiFile shape — record per H2 discipline, sorted alphabetically,
  additive: {source_hash, module_name, exported_entries, imports,
  imports_hashes, handle_count}

  Hash-key invalidation policy — v1 uses source_hash; v2 (future,
  if measured to matter) uses exported_entries hash for finer
  granularity. Conservative-correct first.

  Cross-overlay handle resolution — overlay-walk-on-chase chosen
  over packed-handle bit-encoding. Smaller blast radius (changes
  chase function only); ceiling at ~100 modules where the O(M)
  per chase becomes measurable.

  Cache invalidation by downstream-reach — when M's source hash
  changes, every module that imports M invalidates because their
  recorded imports_hashes for M is now stale.

  LSP didChange wiring shares the driver — same operation, two
  surfaces. cache.ka and driver.ka serve both inka build/check
  AND the LSP's textDocument/didChange handler.

Substrate dependencies all met: H2 records, H3 SchemeKind,
Ω.5 frame records, graph.ka's Salsa 3.0 / overlay shape.
No new substrate primitive required — pure handler-projection.

Scope: ~400-600 lines across cache.ka + driver.ka + LSP wiring,
land as commit cluster (cache first; driver second; LSP third).
Each independently useful at landing.

Verification by simulation per dream-code discipline. Six
walkthrough scenarios: cold compile, no-op edit, leaf-module
edit, core-module edit, public-surface-unchanged, cross-overlay
chase. Each traces what the substrate does without running
wasmtime.

Surprises captured for future: public-surface-vs-source diff
optimization (v2), Reason DAG serialization stability across
compiler versions (cheap fix: compiler_version field in KaiFile),
concurrent didChange ordering (atomic temp+rename), overlay
limit at ~100 modules.

Couples with F.2 LSP arc (Priority 1) — they share the driver
mentl/d9bfe38:
Region = every HandleExpr on Alloc (structural detection by
scanning arms for 'alloc' op; nested handlers produce nested
regions). No naming convention, no attribute markup — the shape
of the handler's arms IS the region marker.

tag_alloc fires at every value-constructing expression
(LMakeClosure, LMakeList, LMakeTuple, LMakeRecord, LMakeVariant,
explicit perform alloc). Tag stores (handle, region_id,
install_span) — install_span carried on the tag directly so
check_escape can diagnose a popped region without a
dead_regions cache.

let-level escape checks flagged as sub-handles (H4.1, H4.2).

Backend is untouched — region tracking is entirely inference-
level. Phase E's emit_memory_arena handles runtime reclamation;
H4's static check is complementary.

sites (mechanical); branch structure mirrors C1's branching
ledger (potential sub-handle); closure capture region lifetime
is transitive (potential second-pass); alloc op's naming becomes
coupling-to-semantics (flagged for post-six refinement).

new alloc sites.

saved .bmrg tapes newest-first and plays one back on the device
through the live game's own presentation - HUD, kill-cam, audio, the
devouring - because the deterministic sim just replays the tape's

drag the bottom strip to scrub, tap a speed, top edge exits. While a
tape rolls the matchbox driver, recorder, rematch gate, bot, and
touch overlays all stand down; the platform input source still runs
but the playback source replaces the LocalInputs map after it.

tier + player kills this match, and the ramp functions extrapolate
past level 4 to saturating ceilings (85% commit charge, 300 cm dodge
bubble, 0.05 rad wobble) - hard forever, aimbot never. Win a match,
the tier climbs; lose, it resets; the practice button carries the
number.

overdriven and settles (the kill finally writes itself onto the
scoreboard), and the decided match's winner holds the CHARGE pose
through the summary. The taunt strip gets a standing on-screen mark
(ring + label, lit while the flex runs) instead of an invisible zone,
and the dash corner, move/throw hints, and zones all follow the new
southpaw setting - the fifth settings row.

The online summary names the winner, carries the rivalry standing,
walks the RUN IT BACK handshake states, and offers the top-band
LEAVE. TWOTOP_AUTOSTART=replays and TWOTOP_AUTOPLAY_TAPE=1 drive
headless capture verification of the new screens.
